observation: plan.md's own headline measurement was wrong: it read Tailwind v4's rounded-full (which compiles to border-radius: calc(infinity * 1px), clamped by the browser to 3.35544e+07px) as an off-scale radius used 99 times, and made that the work package's lead defect statement. combined-round.md's own measurement pass caught it before build: genuinely off-scale radii were 21, not 99; the real defect was that pill has two spellings (rounded-full vs rounded-[var(--r-pill)], 69 vs 87 sites). The plan was planned around a measurement artifact, and the correction only happened because the combined round re-measured from scratch rather than trusting the plan's numbers.

combined-round.md re-derived the plan's numbers independently before building and explicitly recorded the correction ('Correction to record in the plan: ... That reading is wrong'), rather than silently building against the plan's wrong 99-count framing. The corrected number (21 genuine off-scale, 156 pill-spelling occurrences across two spellings) is what actually drove the AC3 fix.

The founder-approved custom procedure (plan.md) specified exactly one review round ('one fresh agent reviews it, one round only... no further human gate after the approval'). It took four rounds (three NOT-DONE, one DONE) to reach acceptance, per progress.json's verdicts array and review.md's three recorded NOT-DONE evaluations. Each of the first three rounds found genuine blocking defects, not nitpicks: round 1 found a Send button computing 17px wide in the running app (B1), 3 of 28 input sites left unmigrated (B2), an unfixed SearchField fill (B3), a status word/treatment mismatch still failing validation scenario 3 (B4), and false claims in tracked files (B5). Round 2 found a live regression re-hidden pill spelling (18 elements computing the off-scale radius). Round 3 found the AC6 backlog had drifted from its own generator (5 sites in 2 files unlisted). The one-round assumption in the approved procedure did not hold for a change of this shape (five closed sets, 124 files, ~14k line diff) and each extra round earned its cost in real defects caught, not style disagreement.

Three of the four review rounds failed the same way: a tracked file (DESIGN.md in round 1, AC3's evidence sentence plus .pipeline/AZ.md and progress.json in round 2, migration-backlog.md in round 3) asserted something the code no longer supported. Round 1: DESIGN.md claimed a type error on an outside-set Button variant that tsc did not actually raise. Round 2: evaluation 1's own AC3 evidence ('rounded-full is no longer generated into the app's CSS') was invalidated by round 1's own @source glob fix, which brought rounded-full back into live CSS and un-hid CommentRow.tsx's two rounded-full sites. Round 3: migration-backlog.md was a generated file that round 2's scanner change (identifier-following) never regenerated, so the committed backlog (44 items) silently diverged from a fresh run of its own generator (46 items), missing 5 sites in 2 files entirely. The orchestrator's own adjudication after evaluation 3 names this pattern explicitly: 'All three rounds failed the same way: a tracked file asserting something the code no longer supports... The recurring failure is that the claims are hand-maintained while the code moves.'

After the third NOT-DONE (the same drift-pattern recurring a third time), the fix was structural rather than a fourth hand-correction: a new mechanical drift guard (tools/repo-gates/src/design-backlog-drift.ts, wired into npm run verify as design:backlog:check) regenerates migration-backlog.md into a scratch location using the real unmodified generator and diffs it against the committed file, failing the build if they disagree. The orchestrator's adjudication after evaluation 3 explicitly names the strategy change: 'Not another manual correction — make the drift mechanically checkable, so a stale backlog fails verification the way an off-scale radius now does.' Round 4 then accepted with no blocking findings.

A pre-existing bug on origin/main (not introduced by AZ7) made the entire design system's utility surface dead CSS: layers/core-ui/src/index.css's @source glob pointed at layers/design-system/src, a path that does not exist (the real package is framework/design-system/src, three directories up). Because Tailwind never scanned it, any class used only inside framework/design-system/src compiled to nothing. Fixing the glob path (commit fe642719, review-fix B1) made +198 CSS rules live with 0 removed, which is what un-hid the Button size="icon" Send control rendering 17px wide instead of 32px (the geometry classes existed only in source, never in shipped CSS) and separately un-hid CommentRow.tsx's rounded-full avatar chrome in round 2.

Review round 1 accepted the claim 'rounded-full is no longer generated into the app's CSS' as AC3 evidence, and that claim was true only as an artifact of the broken @source glob (rounded-full was never generated for anyone, not because AZ7's migration removed it). Once the glob was fixed in the same round's own review-fix pass, the evidence round 1 had relied on was invalidated, and round 2 had to find the newly-live rounded-full sites (CommentRow.tsx) as a fresh blocking finding. Evaluation 1's own AC3 verdict (PASS) was correct given what was true at the time it ran, but became false the moment a different finding from the same round was fixed — a case where a review's evidence had a shorter shelf life than the review round itself.

.pipeline/AZ.md describes AZ-bugs.md as the track's 'main artifact.' The planner reported it missing during AZ7 (per progress.json notes: 'BLOCKER OUTSIDE AZ7... That file does not exist in the worktree or in git history'), then corrected that in the same notes field after finding it does exist on disk (168 lines, ~150 items) in one specific worktree (ui-audit-optimization-8541a2), untracked. Root cause: .gitignore ignores .pipeline/* and re-includes only work-packages/, progress/, retro-log/, audits/, work/, and files matching [A-Z].md or [A-Z][A-Z].md; AZ-bugs.md matches none of those patterns, so git silently ignores it everywhere except the one worktree where it happens to exist on disk. The track's own claimed main artifact is invisible to every worktree that isn't that specific one, and would be permanently lost if that worktree were pruned. progress.json records this as a one-line .gitignore fix, explicitly not AZ7's job.

Each of the four review rounds' verification method was to plant a violation, show the relevant guard go red, then revert it and re-confirm green, rather than reading the rule's source and trusting it works. This is what distinguished real enforcement from claimed enforcement: round 1 found the Button variant type guard (@ts-expect-error on the literal string 'amber') did not fire when a genuine 5th variant was added properly to both the union and VARIANT_CLASSES (B5) — a defect that reading the guard's code alone would not surface, only running the exact scenario it was supposed to catch. Round 2 confirmed the round-1 fix by reproducing the identical break-test and getting a real TS2322 failure. Round 3 went further and planted 8 named perturbation shapes the builder had not authored (const chain, ternary-with-identifier-branches, .join() via const and inline, const inside a nested function, plus 3 deliberate shadowing cases and a .map() arrow-param name collision to check for false positives) against the round-2 enforcement fix, finding zero false positives and confirming the documented boundary (let, imported, runtime-computed values stay unfollowed) matched the code's actual behavior.

review.md contains full write-ups for evaluation rounds 1, 2, and 3 (each with its own blocking/non-blocking sections and AC status table), plus the orchestrator's adjudication after evaluation 3. Round 4's DONE verdict exists only as a short evidence summary inside progress.json's 'review-4' session entry (backlog count, lint config check, radius count, icon geometry, verify/test pass) — no full round-4 review write-up was appended to review.md the way the first three were. The specific perturbation shapes and counts round 4 tested, if any beyond what round 3 already covered, are not recorded anywhere in the artifacts.
